notes: The Hotel Zone R1/R2 bus costs 15 MXN. ADO buses run to Chichén, Tulum and Playa. A hire car gives you freedom for the cenotes (insurance is expensive).
December to April is dry and 28°C, but it is the busiest and priciest period (Christmas, March spring break). November and April are the sweet spot.
Reach Chichén Itzá and Tulum at the 08:00 opening; by midday it is 35°C and tour buses arrive. Non-biodegradable sunscreen is banned in the cenotes.
Hotel Zone restaurants are 3-5 times pricier; Mercado 28 and downtown (Parque de las Palapas) have local prices. Pay in pesos; the dollar rate is poor.
Tip 10-15%; say 'no gracias' to beach vendors. Drink bottled water.
Ferries: Isla Mujeres from Puerto Juárez (Hotel Zone piers are pricier), Cozumel from Playa, Holbox from Chiquilá.

stops.name: Playa Delfines
stops.tips: Cancún's biggest free beach: no hotels, turquoise Caribbean water. Check for sargassum season (May to August).

stops.name: Cancún Sign Playa Delfines
stops.tips: Colourful CANCUN letters, perfect for photos.

stops.name: El Fish Fritanga
stops.tips: Local fish restaurant on the lagoon. Try the ceviche and tikin xic (grilled marinated fish); rare value for the Hotel Zone.

stops.name: Museo Maya de Cancún
stops.tips: Maya museum with the San Miguelito ruins; an air-conditioned afternoon option.

stops.name: Playa Chac Mool
stops.tips: Central public beach for sunset and waves.

backups.name: Mercado 28 Los De Pescado
backups.tips: Fish tacos in the downtown market, a spot for locals.

backups.name: Playa Tortugas
backups.tips: Calm beach on the lagoon side, next to the ferry dock.

stops.name: Ultramar Feribot Puerto Juárez
stops.tips: 20-minute ferry (about 28 USD return). Rent a golf cart on the island (about 800 MXN).

stops.name: Playa Norte
stops.tips: One of the world's best beaches: shallow and calm, loungers 100-200 MXN.

stops.name: Punta Sur Isla Mujeres
stops.tips: The island's southern tip, with the Ixchel temple ruin and a sculpture park. Mexico's first sunrise.

stops.name: Mango Cafe Isla Mujeres
stops.tips: Caribbean breakfast and lunch; the coconut French toast is the island's famous dish.

stops.name: MUSA Underwater Museum Snorkelling
stops.tips: 500 underwater sculptures. Snorkelling tours leave from the pier; catch the 17:30 ferry back.

backups.name: Isla Mujeres Mercado Municipal
backups.tips: Cheap local food at the municipal market.

backups.name: Garrafón Reef Park
backups.tips: Zipline and snorkelling park, an alternative to MUSA.

stops.name: Chichén Itzá
stops.tips: 2.5 hours from Cancún (ADO bus or tour). See the Kukulkan pyramid and ball court; at the 08:00 opening it is cool and empty. Entry about 697 MXN.

stops.name: Cenote Ik Kil
stops.tips: 5 minutes from Chichén. An open cenote 26 m deep with hanging vines; life jacket compulsory.

stops.name: Valladolid Casa Tía Micha
stops.tips: Yucatán cuisine in Valladolid: cochinita pibil (slow-roasted pork) and sopa de lima (lime soup).

stops.name: Valladolid Calzada de los Frailes
stops.tips: Pastel-coloured colonial street leading to the Convent of San Bernardino.

stops.name: Cenote Suytun
stops.tips: Cave cenote with a famous beam of light; best in afternoon light. The return trip takes 2 hours.

backups.name: Cenote Zací Valladolid
backups.tips: A cenote in the town itself, instead of Suytun.

backups.name: El Mesón del Marqués Valladolid
backups.tips: Colonial restaurant on the main square.

stops.name: Tulum Ruins
stops.tips: 2 hours from Cancún. A Maya fortress by the sea, opening at 08:00; entry about 95 MXN plus a parking fee. Look out for iguanas.

stops.name: Playa Ruinas Tulum
stops.tips: The beach below the ruins, good for a short swim.

stops.name: Gran Cenote
stops.tips: Cave cenote for snorkelling, with turtles and stalactites. The water is clearest in the morning.

stops.name: Taquería Honorio Tulum
stops.tips: Tulum's legendary breakfast and lunch taco spot; cochinita and lechón (suckling pig), sold out by 14:00.

stops.name: Tulum Beach Road
stops.tips: Palm-lined coast road. Choose a beach club (Papaya Playa) or a public beach (Playa Paraíso).

backups.name: Cenote Dos Ojos
backups.tips: A cave system with two "eyes", instead of Gran Cenote.

backups.name: Antojitos La Chiapaneca
backups.tips: Al pastor in Tulum town; an evening stop.

stops.name: Xcaret Park
stops.tips: Underground rivers, a Maya village and an evening show (about 150 USD). 1 hour from Cancún; lunch is included in the Plus package.

stops.name: Xcaret Buffet
stops.tips: Buffet inside the park, included in the Plus package.

stops.name: Xcaret México Espectacular
stops.tips: A show on Mexican history with 300 performers; included in the park ticket.

backups.name: El Fogón Playa del Carmen
backups.tips: Al pastor tacos in Playa, as an alternative to the park.

stops.name: Chiquilá Ferry Holbox
stops.tips: 2.5 hours from Cancún plus a 20-minute ferry. A car-free island.

stops.name: Holbox Punta Cocos
stops.tips: Shallow, warm lagoon with flamingos and hammock bars.

stops.name: Holbox Roots Pizza
stops.tips: Lobster pizza on Holbox.

stops.name: Holbox Punta Mosquito Sandbar
stops.tips: A sandbar you can walk to at low tide. Come for sunset, or a whale shark tour from May to September.

backups.name: Isla Contoy Tour
backups.tips: Bird island with snorkelling off Isla Mujeres, instead of Holbox or Cozumel.

stops.name: Mercado 28
stops.tips: Downtown crafts market: hammocks and silver, with 40% haggling room.

stops.name: Cocina La Chaya Mercado 28
stops.tips: Yucatán home cooking: panuchos (stuffed fried tortillas) and chaya juice. A farewell meal.

stops.name: Parque de las Palapas
stops.tips: Downtown square with marquesitas (crispy crepes) stalls in the evening; quiet by day.

stops.name: ADO Airport Bus
stops.tips: ADO from downtown to the airport takes 30 minutes; time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Taquería Los Charros Cancún
backups.tips: Tacos downtown, instead of the market.

backups.name: Playa Langosta
backups.tips: One last swim in the Hotel Zone.
